title: UNTP 0.7.0 credentials secured with JOSE, pilot exchange profile
description: A pilot interoperability profile for the UN Transparency Protocol's 0.7.0 release, tagged v0.7.0 on 4 May 2026 at the specification's GitLab home: product passport, traceability event and conformity credentials in the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0, secured as compact JWS under VC-JOSE-COSE, mapped to and from native evidence with every loss visible. The schema and context artefacts are pinned by digest from that tag. UNTP compatibility is a distinct claim from any regulatory conformance, and verification by UNTP's own test tooling is a further claim this profile does not make.
dataModel: W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 with the UNTP 0.7.0 vocabularies

artefacts.notes: The 0.7.0 release, tagged v0.7.0 on 4 May 2026 at the GitLab home (main last active 4 September 2026, revision df03d8f87e74f676ccfece87ba77cd8f804fe111). The GitHub repository uncefact/spec-untp is archived at 0.6.1 and points here. No 1.0 release exists. The documentation site untp.unece.org refuses non-browser clients, so the tag is the pinnable source; the specification text is many pages and carries no single digest, and the four artefacts below are pinned individually.

The DigitalProductPassport JSON Schema at v0.7.0, 50362 bytes. Its published location https://untp.unece.org/artefacts/schema/v0.7.0/dpp/DigitalProductPassport.json answered 403 to a non-browser client on 2026-09-06. The schema defines credentialStatus as a BitstringStatusListEntry, renderMethod and issuingSoftware beside the credential subject; a credential validated against it names the UNTP context.

proofSuites.keyRule: The issuer's secp256k1 credential key, published under its DID as an assertion method; verified independently with a second JOSE library.
proofSuites.notes: A JOSE library that omits ES256K is a compatibility limit, not a signature defect. UNTP's own test suite (uncefact/tests-untp, technical interoperability, verifiable credentials) verifies enveloping proofs with EdDSA on Ed25519 under a did:web issuer and a Bitstring status entry, and names no other algorithm, so a credential secured under this suite is not verifiable by that tooling; a consumer that requires the tooling's verification needs an Ed25519 signing capability this profile does not define.

proofSuites.keyRule: A dedicated P-256 credential key, separately authorised and published with its relationship to the issuer and to the BSV actor. Never derived by the secp256k1 BRC-42 rule; never an ES256K signature relabelled.

anchoring.bytesCommitted: the exact compact JWS bytes as issued
anchoring.subjectRule: one product identifier the credential signs; a multi-product credential names the selected one
anchoring.attestationType: UNTP-DPP, UNTP-DTE or UNTP-DCC by credential type

nativeEvidenceExtension.notes: A credential that references existing native evidence carries the extension under urn:bsv:dpp:native-evidence:1; the native evidence exists first and the credential is signed over the references, so no digest is circular.

mappings.externalEvent: product passport issuance; a manufacture traceability event only with manufacturing evidence
mappings.requires: manufacturing facility, time and responsible party for a manufacture event

mappings.externalEvent: a transformation or transaction event only with actual movement or custody evidence
mappings.requires: source, destination and custody evidence; a change of token control is not a shipment

mappings.externalEvent: a change of custody only with custody evidence
mappings.requires: custody evidence beyond the token transfer

mappings.externalEvent: a traceability event of the repair, with the repair facts
mappings.requires: what was done, by whom and when

mappings.externalEvent: a revised product passport credential; no physical event
an end-of-life traceability event, distinguishing disposition from a process whose outputs carry new identities

storage.nativeClaim: the signed dpp-lifecycle-v1 object, when the event has one
storage.originalSecured: the exact compact JWS as issued, with mediaType, byteLength, sha256, credentialId, issuer, receivedAt, schemaRefs and the intake report reference
storage.projection: any derived document, with its own identity and exporter signature, naming its source

unsupported.reason: Selected only when a real restricted-disclosure use case names it; ordinary JSON filtering is not cryptographic selective disclosure.
UNTP compatibility is a distinct claim from EU regulatory conformance, which needs the applicable legal instrument and its date.
No 1.0 release exists (checked 2026-09-06 at the GitLab home); this profile pins the 0.7.0 tag and moves only by a new profile version.

UNTP's test suite verifies EdDSA (Ed25519) enveloping proofs under did:web issuers only; the ES256K credentials this profile secures fail its securing-mechanism check before schema or context are examined. Passing that tooling is a separate claim needing an Ed25519 signing key and a did:web issuer, neither defined here.
